title: 2007 HMMT February General Round 1 Problem 9
statement: I have four distinct rings that I want to wear on my right hand hand (five distinct fingers.) One of these rings is a Canadian ring that must be worn on a finger by itself, the rest I can arrange however I want. If I have two or more rings on the same finger, then I consider different orders of rings along the same finger to be different arrangements. How many different ways can I wear the rings on my fingers?

solutions.text: 600. First we pick the finger for the Canadian ring. This gives a multiplicative factor of 5 . For distributing the remaining 3 rings among 4 fingers, they can either be all on the same finger ( \(4 \cdot 3\) ! ways), all on different fingers \(\left(\binom{4}{3} \cdot 3\right.\) ! ways), or two on one finger and one on another \(\left(4 \cdot\binom{3}{2} \cdot 2!\cdot 3\right.\) ways.) Therefore, I have \(5 \cdot(24+24+72)=600\) choices.
